findings.title: Datasource keying statement overgeneralised
findings.problem: The guide says datasource PUTs are keyed by (project_name, name), not by id, but the provider PUT in the same diff is addressed by id (/v1/index/provider/idx-1, test patches IndexInfo.find_by_id). The doc's headline 're-sending the same body leaves the entity unchanged' is also stronger than its own rows (error reset on google/git_faq/file, ciphertext change on non-deterministic backends).
findings.impact: Readers and clients take the guide as contract; it misdescribes pinned behaviour. Provider route finding was not independently confirmed against src (reachability unconfirmed).
findings.recommendation: Qualify the row: name the provider route as id-addressed and scope the idempotency guarantee to the exceptions listed in the table.

findings.title: Skill no-new-version test is vacuous
findings.problem: test_reput_without_content_change_adds_no_version filters stored Skill row keys containing 'version' and compares first vs second. The Skill model has no version-like column, so both sides are {} and the assertion can never fail.
findings.impact: The test reads as proof that a skill re-PUT creates no version but passes regardless of behaviour; a versioning regression would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Assert against a real signal (e.g. a version table or content/updated state), or drop the test; at minimum assert the filtered dict is non-empty.

findings.title: Idempotency tests violate Module Cohesion
findings.problem: A new concern (idempotent PUT tests with idem_* fixtures, IdemCase, sqlite JSONB shim; lines 1479-2075) is appended to an already ~2000-line router test file, breaking the code-quality Module Cohesion standard.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard is broken and the file grows well past the ~500-line threshold; also duplicates a global JSONB sqlite compile hook and wipes dependency_overrides on teardown.
findings.recommendation: Move the block into its own module, e.g. test_index_idempotent_write.py, importing shared helpers from idempotency_helpers.py.
